summary.title: Build Your own Simplified AngularJS in 200 Lines of JavaScript
summary.one_liner: You learn how AngularJS's core ideas (dependency injection, DOM compilation via DFS, scopes and dirty-checking digest loops) fit together by building a simplified "Lightweight AngularJS" in about 200 lines.
keywords: how does angularjs work under the hood
eval and with in javascript expressions
takeaways: Re-implementing a simplified model of a framework is an effective way to learn its core principles.
The Provider combines $provide and $injector: it registers components, resolves dependencies by parsing parameter names, and caches singletons.
The DOMCompiler walks the DOM depth-first, finds attribute-based directives, and calls their link functions with the right scope.
Scopes store watchers; $digest repeatedly evaluates watched expressions until stable, then recurses into child scopes.
The implementation uses eval and with for expression evaluation and has no circular dependency handling, so it is for education only, not production.
summary.summary: The article walks through building a simplified 'Lightweight AngularJS' framework to explain how AngularJS works. It defines three core parts: a Provider (registration, dependency resolution and initialization), a DOMCompiler (depth-first traversal of the DOM to find and link directives), and a Scope (watchers plus a dirty-checking $digest loop). It also introduces the graph-theory background used (DFS and the component, DOM and scope graphs) and shows code for ngl-bind, ngl-model and ngl-controller. The author is explicit that the code is educational, uses eval and with, and does not handle circular dependencies.
